subject: SLA carveout: reserved GPU throughput & queueing fallback
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@calyxhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@calyxhealth.com, Michelle Turner <mturner@calyxhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity SLA questions / queueing fallback during nightly batch windows

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Calyx is close to a procurement decision but Legal and Engineering raised two specific items we need clarified before we move to an LOI:

1) Throughput guarantee mechanics for reserved GPUs — our workload mixes short interactive queries (median 120 tokens) during business hours and large nightly batch jobs (10k+ token sequences) that run at 02:00 local time. We need a clear carveout so batch jobs do not penalize the interactive SLA.

2) Queueing behavior and fallback — how request routing behaves when reserved GPUs are saturated; specifically: preemption/backpressure behavior, queue depth limits per-tenant, and whether warm standby (burst to shared capacity) incurs different latency guarantees or credits.

I've attached a small traffic profile (.zip) that shows our hourly distribution and two sample traces. Procurement would also like the proposed credit formula spelled out.

Can you put together a short note + an updated draft SLA that addresses those two items? Would prefer to have this in writing before we loop Legal into a redline pass.

Thanks,

Rajiv Menon
Director, Platform Engineering
Calyx Healthtech

Attachments: traffic_profile_calyx_aug.zip (archive, 1 file)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@calyxhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLA questions / queueing fallback during nightly batch windows

Rajiv —

Appreciate the traffic dump — this is exactly the kind of signal we need. Short version in case you want a one-pager for your stakeholders:

- Reserved GPU sizing: for the profile you sent we recommend an initial reservation of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (configurable). That maps to a steady-state interactive throughput target of approximately 800 concurrent short requests (roughly ~1,500 r/s peak across the pool) with a 99.9th percentile tail target for inference latency of <= 700ms for prompt+generation up to 2k tokens.

- Nightly batch carveout: we will classify scheduled batch windows and route them to a separate "batch lane" inside the reserved pool. Batch jobs will be rate-limited so they cannot evict interactive requests during your business hours (08:00–20:00 ET). Overnight (00:00–06:00 ET) batch can use excess reserved capacity and burst into shared capacity (if configured) but with different latency SLOs (best-effort) and no credit accrual for those tokens.

- Queueing & fallback behavior: when the reserved pool reaches queue-depth thresholds we will: (a) apply backpressure to batch lanes first, (b) accept interactive requests into a short-lived in-memory queue (configurable max 2s wait), and (c) if steady overload persists, we execute staged fallback: redirect new interactive requests to a pinned compatible model on shared capacity (warm standby). Warm standby has the same model weights but a different execution profile; latency SLOs will be the documented fallback SLOs (typically 2x tail latency vs reserved pool).

I've kept high-level language here — Marissa will follow up with procurement-friendly wording and a credit example sheet (how credits scale with minutes of degraded capacity). Lauren, can you confirm the fallback SLO multiplier and whether an explicit per-tenant queue-depth cap is required?

If this plan looks acceptable, I can draft the updated SLA (short memo + tracked redlines) by EOD tomorrow. Otherwise let's take 30 mins to align.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: —

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@calyxhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, procurement@calyxhealth.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLA questions / queueing fallback during nightly batch windows

Rajiv / team —

Thanks, Karthik — adding procurement detail and a concrete credit example. High level items I've baked into the draft:

- Credit calculation (example): monthly committed spend multiplied by percentage of minutes below target during business hours; credits capped at 50% of monthly committed spend per event and 100% per month total. Line-item in sheet: minutes_breached -> %credit. (See attached SLA_Calculation_Table.xlsx)

- Maintenance & scheduled downtime: Redwood will provide a 72-hour calendar notice for non-emergency maintenance that affects the reserved pool. Emergency maintenance will be limited to <60 minutes and compensated per the credit table.

- Carveout for batch: we've added a definition section: "Batch lane" (= scheduled large sequence work). Batch requests are explicitly rate-limited during business hours and will not be counted toward interactive SLA calculations.

- Queue-depth cap: default 500 requests across the pool; per-tenant caps are configurable on request — note that smaller per-tenant caps may reduce headroom for bursty customers.

Next steps: if Calyx can confirm desired monthly committed spend band and preferred rescue behavior (warm standby vs immediate drop to shared capacity), we can produce a tracked-redline SLA.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Calculation_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 file)

From: Michelle Turner <mturner@calyxhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@calyxhealth.com>, procurement@calyxhealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLA questions / queueing fallback during nightly batch windows

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick responses. A few items Legal would like captured in the SLA redline:

- Explicit statement that during business hours (08:00–20:00 ET) Redwood will not preempt interactive requests from the reserved pool to serve other tenants without prior written consent. We are open to limited soft-preemption only for documented safety/security events.

- Queueing behavior must include a clear maximum wait time (we propose 2s as above) and an escalation contact if requests are dropped.

- Fallback SLOs should be expressed numerically (e.g., 99th percentile latency on fallback <= X ms) rather than as a multiplier where possible. If you cannot provide exact numbers for fallback latency, please provide a deterministic method for measuring/benchmarking them.

- We will circulate a single tracked-redline document (legal + technical) for sign-off. Please include a clause on how credits are calculated for prolonged degraded windows (more than 60 minutes).

Attaching a short list of initial redlines (PDF).

Michelle Turner
Senior Counsel, Calyx Healthtech

Attachments: redlines_calyx_v1.pdf (pdf, 1 file)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Turner <mturner@calyxhealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <r.menon@calyxhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLA questions / queueing fallback during nightly batch windows

Michelle / Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick technical clarifications and proposals so Legal can redline deterministically:

- No soft-preemption during business hours: we can commit to "no non-emergency eviction of interactive requests from the customer's reserved pool between 08:00–20:00 ET". Emergency maintenance is defined in the maintenance section and will trigger the emergency credit path.

- Quantitative fallback SLOs: for the warm-standby fallback we can guarantee a measured 99th percentile tail latency <= 1.4s for interactive requests with prompt+response <= 2k tokens, under conditions where shared capacity latency is measured in our internal benchmarking for the pinned model. We will publish the test harness and reproducible benchmark steps (link to Drive). If Calyx requires tighter numbers we can scope a performance test during PO stage.

- Queueing caps & behavior: default pool queue-depth cap = 500 requests; per-tenant cap configurable to a minimum of 50 requests. Max enqueued wait time for interactive requests = 2s (configurable). If a request is dropped due to queue overflow, an incident will be logged and the customer will be notified via the priority channel (integration with your PagerDuty or Slack webhook).

- Credits for prolonged events: we will adopt Marissa's example table but add a progressive multiplier for events > 60 minutes (to reflect operational impact). We'll surface concrete examples in the draft.

Next steps: I'll upload an updated draft SLA (tracked) to the shared Drive with the changes above and a redline-ready area for your legal team. Proposed meeting: Thu 09/03 10:00 ET to review redlines and run a brief Q&A with our runtime engineer (30 min). If that works I will send an invite.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-dedicated-sla-draft-v2.pdf (draft SLA, tracked changes)
